reason: E4 and E5 directly demonstrate a 5-minute reheating step at ~1100 K followed by rapid cooling to achieve a disorder-to-order transition in multi-element nanoparticles, supporting the core premises. However, the hypothesis overstates the generality by claiming a single-phase solid solution rather than the ordered intermetallic (MPEI) structure actually produced, and E3 highlights segregation risks under rapid cooling that are not fully addressed.
premises: A 5-minute dwell at ~1100 K enables a disorder-to-order transition in noble-metal HEA nanoparticles
Rapid cooling (~10^4 K/s) kinetically traps the ordered single-phase solid solution
Deviations from the 5-minute dwell cause phase separation, segregation, or uncontrolled morphology
The disorder-to-order transition lowers Gibbs free energy of the ordered state
Limited atomic mobility during the dwell is the key kinetic control parameter
